prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph shot at high noon on an overcast volcanic plain, 24mm medium-format camera, low-contrast flat grey sky. Black basalt ground strewn with loose scoria.

Subject:
A single obsidian spire, roughly 800 meters tall, rises from the plain and curves slightly like a black glass claw. The surface is mirror-polished volcanic glass reflecting the overcast sky; fresh chipped edges reveal deep charcoal interior. Near the tip, the spire tapers to a razor edge that catches a single pinprick of sun breaking through clouds.

Important details:
Hyper-realistic obsidian — specular highlight rolls along the curved surface; conchoidal fracture patches show rainbow oil-slick sheen. Tiny science-expedition drone in the sky for scale, one-to-one-hundred-thousandth the spire height. The overcast sky diffuses shadows almost completely, but the spire casts a long soft grey band across the basalt plain due to its sheer height. Ground texture: sharp volcanic glass shards and fine ash.

Use case:
Crystal-studies single 3/5 — impossible monolithic obsidian spire emphasizing scale and mirror-surface material.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no dragons or creatures, no stylized illustration, no heavy color grading, no visible brand on the drone.
